summary: Adrenal venous sampling for lateralization of aldosterone secretion in surgically eligible primary hyperaldosteronism.

items: Biochemically confirmed primary hyperaldosteronism.
Patient is a candidate for adrenalectomy.
Goal is to lateralize aldosterone secretion before operative planning.

short and small; enters the posterolateral IVC, often near T11-T12 and above the right renal vein.
usually joins the inferior phrenic vein; their common trunk enters the superior aspect of the left renal vein.
small accessory hepatic veins near the right adrenal ostium can look similar on venography.
duplicated adrenal veins or a shared hepatic-adrenal trunk can alter sampling and dilute hormone concentrations.
an infrarenal IVC or peripheral venous sample provides the comparator for adrenal hormone measurements.
review venous imaging, cosyntropin timing, collection tubes, and the laboratory's labeling and rapid-cortisol workflow.
use ultrasound-guided femoral access and prepare the IVC/peripheral reference sampling route.
use gentle, low-volume venography to confirm the ostium; avoid deep wedging. Cone-beam CT can clarify uncertain anatomy.
enter through the left renal vein and confirm the common adrenal-phrenic trunk.
clear catheter dead space per protocol, then gently sample both adrenal veins and the reference site for aldosterone and cortisol; record site, time, and stimulation status.
use rapid cortisol when available; adrenal/reference cortisol ratio is commonly >=5 with cosyntropin or >=2 without it. Apply local criteria and resample if inadequate.
verify specimens before sheath removal, obtain hemostasis, and send results for cortisol-corrected aldosterone comparison and endocrine interpretation.
an accessory hepatic vein can mimic the right adrenal vein; confirm selectivity rather than trusting the venogram alone.
avoid forceful injection and deep wedging; stop and assess new flank/back pain, extravasation, or instability.
a deep tributary may miss tumor drainage and falsely suggest the opposite side; sample representative gland outflow.
strong suction can collapse the vein; aspirate gently and reassess catheter position instead of pulling harder.
clear contrast/flush dead space, label tubes immediately, and keep sampling times and cosyntropin status consistent.
confirm bilateral selectivity first; compare aldosterone/cortisol ratios, not raw aldosterone. Cortisol cosecretion can confound interpretation.
